claims.statement: Supabase keys applied migrations on the numeric version string (the filename prefix), which is why renaming a recorded file makes `db push` re-run it against a database that already has its objects, and why hand-applied SQL leaves the database ahead of its own records.

Editing an already-recorded migration changes the repository and never the database, because the recorded version still matches and nothing re-runs; ADR-007 therefore ships as a new additive file whose statements are individually guarded and re-runnable, and it is correct whichever way the applied/unapplied question about 20260910120000 lands.

`apply_migration` assigns its own recorded version string, so the file was renamed to match the version actually recorded; the standing advice is to check the version the MCP tool recorded and rename to match rather than let a recorded version dangle.

`20261024110000_add_dashboard_operational_fields` is a standing hazard: its `batches.billing_deadline` column is live while its version is unrecorded and the rest of the file unverified, so it is an applied column with an unapplied file and a `db push` would try to re-run it.

`public.tenants` carries a live policy "Tenants selectable by Clerk user" that no migration in the directory defines, and it omits the `is_active` check, so the checked-in policy map describes intent rather than every policy currently enforcing the table.

Regeneration of `lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is only safe against a database that already holds every object the file describes, because generator output is a snapshot of one database; the file has never been regenerated, is hand-maintained, and is wrong in both directions (it carries `billing_deadline` ahead of its record and omits `excused`, `max_absence_percent`, five tables and `billing_type`).

Migration SQL with no ledger row is the unreproducible case: hand-applied objects exist and are recorded by hand but a rebuild from the migrations would omit them — concretely `batches.billing_deadline`, the undefined `tenants` policy, and the T2MIS validation work, whose version was inserted into `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` by hand after a piecemeal apply.

To confirm a migration landed, its objects are checked by name (`pg_proc` for functions, `pg_policies` for policies) rather than by comparing policy sets, because several migrations add policies to the same tables and a set comparison returns a superset that always reads as a match.

The `app_private.*` helper chain is all `security definer` with `search_path = ''` and resolves identity from `auth.jwt() ->> 'sub'` alone, then role from `profiles.role`, threading `profiles.is_active` through `current_profile_id` and `can_access_tenant` so a deactivated profile drops access at the next request.

`platform_admins` has RLS enabled and deliberately no policy; the deny comes entirely from RLS-with-no-policies rather than withheld grants, so the linter's `rls_enabled_no_policy` finding is the design, and `public.current_user_is_platform_admin()` (boolean about the caller only) is the only read path.

The platform admin's reach is the school registry only: `is_platform_admin()` appears on `tenants`, `qualifications`, `tenant_qualifications`, unassigned `profiles` and `profile_tenant_memberships`, and extending it to a compliance table or letting it seat itself into a tenant is a boundary change needing its own ADR (RULES.md rule 30).

Seating a tenant's first member requires both `profile_id <> current_profile_id()` and "the tenant has no members yet"; the first closes self-escalation through `can_access_tenant`, which resolves purely from memberships, and the second is racy but tolerable only because the first holds.

The first-member policy's subquery depends on the `profile_tenant_memberships` select policy: narrowing "Platform admins can read tenant memberships" makes an already-occupied tenant read as empty and silently weakens the insert policy.

`create_school` is `security invoker` on purpose — it exists for transactionality so a school and its program list land together, and RLS still evaluates every statement inside it, so a non-platform-admin caller gets a policy violation rather than a privilege.
`ensure_profile_tenant_membership` is the only function in the history granted to `service_role` rather than `authenticated`, because its caller is the Clerk webhook, which has no session.

The base migration enables RLS on all 14 of its tables and the later files do so for every table they create, so `platform_admins`, `learner_identities` and every other table is RLS-governed rather than grant-governed.

`billing_records` gets select and insert policies only; the absence of update and delete policies is what makes the generation log append-only, and its select spells `admin`/`coordinator`/`viewer` out by name to keep trainers from financial rows while leaving viewer read access.

Trainer trimming is enforced by RLS on `learner_details`: its select policy names admin, coordinator and viewer only and its comment says trainers are deliberately absent, so the T2MIS personal and employment fields sit in their own one-to-one table because RLS filters rows and not columns.

`batches` admittance is asymmetric by verb: select uses `can_read_batch(id)` so an assigned trainer can read their own batch, while all three write policies use `can_manage_tenant(tenant_id)`, so no trainer can write a batch row.

Admin user provisioning is admin-only rather than admin+coordinator even though `can_manage_tenant` would have admitted coordinators, and the grant policy requires `can_access_tenant(tenant_id)` so an admin of one school cannot grant access to another.

The `EXISTS` subqueries in the profile, membership and trainer-credential policies are RLS-filtered by `profile_tenant_memberships`' own select policy, so the same-tenant predicate cannot resolve a school the caller cannot see.

The base migration seeds the three tenants, the two scholarship programs, the document catalog and the billing rules, so that seed being recorded-applied is part of what makes it canonical, and `supabase/seed.sql` stays a stub because the initial migration inserts the data.

The schema carries eight enums, seven created by the base migration and `billing_type` by the billing-domain migration, while `database.types.ts` lists only seven and omits `billing_type`; rule 18's total `DB_TO_UI_STAGE` map keeps a new variant failing compilation rather than drifting silently.

`batches.billing_deadline` degrades to "not recorded" rather than `undefined` because the mapper reads `row.billing_deadline ?? null` and `tests/unit/batches.test.ts` pins the absent-column case to a null deadline and an infinite `daysToBilling`.
`database.types.ts` is imported only by module `data/` layers: `eslint.config.mjs` restricts the raw row types away from `app/`, `shared/`, `modules/*/ui` and `modules/*/domain`.
`learners` is uniquely keyed on `(tenant_id, batch_id, uli)` through a `create unique index` with no dedup step, so a batch already holding one ULI twice fails the file and rolls it back.
